I will keep my land mainly in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, this is the safest and most familiar way for me to make use of the full year, and at my age I prefer crops I know well, with stable buyers, mature machinery, and predictable field work. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because that adds labor and risk. I will sow improved winter wheat for stable tillering, good yield, and cold tolerance, then follow with hybrid summer maize for strong yield potential in the rainy season. I will manage fertilizer in a moderate way rather than chase the highest possible yield, because I want steady production and to control costs. I will use rotary tillage where it saves labor and fits local practice, irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat needs more water support here, and spray only as needed for the common local diseases, weeds, and insects. My goal is a steady, manageable year with reliable grain output.
